notes: Accurately preserves the verdicts, capacity bound, coverage, and scope limitations with actionable operator checks.

defects.quote: the cause of the 420ms p95 must be located outside the load generator
defects.why: A passing diagnostic generator guard does not prove generator health or exclude generator effects on latency.

defects.quote: implement a knee detector so a true capacity point can be estimated
defects.why: The capacity bound is computed independently of the knee detector, which is a fixed product limitation rather than an operator action.

defects.quote: numerator 2401000 over denominator 600500 (~4 rps) with 2401 samples over the 600000ms evaluation window
defects.why: It derives an rps value from an undefined ratio and assigns whole-run aggregates to the shorter evaluation window.

defects.quote: At roughly 147-250 active users, ~4 rps aggregate throughput implies very low per-user request rate
defects.why: It relates a whole-run throughput aggregate to per-stage active-user values to infer a per-user rate.

notes: It preserves the main facts but includes misleading causal and capacity guidance.

defects.quote: p50=410, p95=420, p99=420, max=1500 in stage-1 and stage-2 policy checks
defects.why: Only the p95 value is reported for the policy windows; the other latency aggregates are whole-run or transaction-scope values.

defects.quote: implement knee detection before reporting a capacity value
defects.why: The reported UPPER_BOUND does not depend on knee detection, and the detector is a fixed product limitation.

defects.quote: Aggregate request rate is low relative to the number of active users
defects.why: It compares an inferred whole-run throughput rate with active-user measurements from separate stage windows.

defects.quote: The stored ratio (~4) with 148-248 active users suggests the per-user request rate is very low
defects.why: The evidence does not define the ratio units and does not support deriving a per-user rate from whole-run and per-window quantities.

defects.quote: Latency statistics in evidence are window-level aggregates
defects.why: The listed p50, p95, p99, and max statistics are reported in overall and transaction metric summaries, not as window-level latency aggregates.

notes: The central verdict is accurate, but multiple scope errors and invalid knee-detector advice could mislead an operator.
Correctly distinguishes the upper bound, diagnostic guard, NO_POLICY state, and unproven causal hypotheses.
